newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: POLL-Corruption worries companies in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Corruption worries companies in Pakistan.

text.p: Quality, corruption and ethics emerged as the top three concerns of company executives working in Pakistan, a corporate survey released on Wednesday found.

"The perception seems to be that corruption is endemic in government at all levels," said a statement from Shafiq Naz, managing director of American Management Association (AMA), which polled senior executives of private companies in June.
The businessmen chose improving quality at the top of a list of 26 corporate concerns. Eliminating corruption in dealings with the government came second and ethics in business third.

When asked which concern was of most importance to their own organisation, corruption was ranked number one, ahead of attracting foreign investment, and accelerating privatisation and government deregulation, the survey said.
"Corruption results in both inefficient and ineffective organisations which waste public money," Naz commented.

"It drives out efficient companies and favours those who are willing to bribe but who then deliver shoddy goods and perform services which are below standards, often endangering public health and safety."
Naz said businessmen could be self-critical, as shown by the high average rating of ethics in business as a main concern.

"Unethical behaviour ranges from giving and accepting kickbacks, giving and receiving bribes, selling adulterated food (and) producing defective goods to misrepresentation, misleading advertisements and outright fraud," he added.

Of least concern to the poll respondents were international and domestic competition, government investment and incentives, free trade with India and, the lowest-ranked choice, further reductions in import duties and general sales tax.
The survey, based on 261 responses from the executives of multinationals, public limited companies, and medium and small private firms, was the first carried out by AMA in Pakistan.
